summary: Zambia waived visas for 43 countries in 2022 and 53 more from January 2025, so 167 nationalities, including the US, UK and the EU, now enter visa-free for up to 90 days in any 12 months. Most others can buy a visa on arrival or apply online, and about 50 nationalities need approval before travel; the KAZA UniVisa adds seamless travel with Zimbabwe around Victoria Falls.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Neighboring countries may in turn ask for a certificate when you arrive from Zambia. Check onward requirements.

source.name: UK FCDO — Zambia travel advice, entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: Not an entry requirement, but recommended — good private care exists in Lusaka, while safari areas rely on air evacuation.

onwardTicket.text: If you arrive by air you must hold a valid return ticket. This applies to visa-free visitors as well as visa holders.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published. If you arrive by land or water you must have enough money for your stay in Zambia and your departure.

source.name: Zambia Department of Immigration — Nationals Who Do Not Require Visa

currencyLimits.text: Travelers carrying more than about USD 5,000 (or the equivalent) in cash should declare it on arrival and departure. Confirm the current threshold with the Zambia Revenue Authority.

source.name: Zambia Department of Immigration

notes: Drones require prior authorization from the Zambia Civil Aviation Authority. Bring the permit or expect the drone to be held at customs.

payments.text: Cards work in Lusaka and Livingstone hotels, supermarkets and fuel stations; markets and rural areas are cash-only. US dollars are widely accepted for safaris and visas, but bring newer-series notes in good condition.

safety.text: Travel in the larger cities and the main game parks is generally safe by day, but serious crime, including vehicle crime, does happen, especially after dark. Demonstrations in Lusaka and other towns can turn violent. Roads are dangerous, with frequent fatal crashes, and wild animals are a real risk on safari and around Victoria Falls.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Zambia travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: May to October is the dry season — prime safari time, hot from September. Victoria Falls thunders fullest from about February to May; by late October the Zambian side can run nearly dry, when the Zimbabwean side keeps more water.

tips.text: Visiting both sides of Victoria Falls? The KAZA UniVisa (USD 50 on arrival at Livingstone or the falls borders) covers Zambia and Zimbabwe for 30 days with unlimited crossings, plus day trips to Botswana via Kazungula — usually cheaper than separate visas.

Victoria Falls is seasonal: spectacular spray February–May, while by October–November the Zambian side can be a trickle — that's when Devil's Pool trips run, and the Zimbabwean side offers better views.
Malaria is present in most of the country year-round, including Livingstone and the safari valleys. Take prophylaxis, use repellent and sleep under nets.
Avoid intercity driving after dark — unlit trucks, pedestrians and animals on the road cause most serious accidents. Distances are long, so plan fuel stops and start early.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Zambia?
faq.answer: Most tourists don't. Zambia waived visas for 43 countries in 2022 and 53 more from 1 January 2025, bringing the visa-exempt list to 167 nationalities, including the US, UK, EU members, Canada, Australia and Japan. Tourists may stay up to 90 days in any 12 months. Most other nationalities can get a visa on arrival or online through the official Zambia Immigration e-services portal; about 50 must have it approved before travel.

faq.question: What is the KAZA UniVisa?
faq.answer: A joint Zambia–Zimbabwe visa costing USD 50, valid 30 days, sold on arrival at Lusaka and Livingstone airports and the Victoria Falls borders to a wide list of nationalities. It allows unlimited crossings between the two countries and day trips into Botswana through Kazungula — ideal for seeing both sides of the falls.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Zambia?
faq.answer: Visa-free visitors may spend up to 90 days in Zambia in any 12 months, counted from the day of first entry. Officers may not grant all 90 days at once; the rest can be added free of charge at an immigration office. Business visitors are limited to 30 days in 12 months (UK FCDO).

faq.question: How do I get a Zambia eVisa and what does it cost?
faq.answer: Apply at eservices.zambiaimmigration.gov.zm with a passport scan and photo. Single-entry visas cost about USD 25 and are normally approved within 3–5 working days. Apply at least a week before travel and carry a printed copy.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Zambia?
faq.answer: Only if you arrive from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Note the reverse trip matters too: some neighbors and onward destinations may ask for a certificate from travelers who passed through parts of Zambia. Check your whole route.
